Episode 05 · Vesper Station

THE LAST JOULE

A blackout. A sealed blast door. One cart at the top of a rail. Every joule counts, and friction wants its share.

Gravitational potential energyWork done by frictionKinetic energyEfficiencyGrades 9–12
CHAPTER 1

CHAPTER 01 · THE MISSION

Will every joule reach the door?

Maya’s plan: let the cart run down the rail, catch it with the recovery flywheel, and turn its energy into one electrical pulse for the door. Predict before you calculate: will all of the cart’s gravitational potential energy end up at the door?

CHAPTER 02 · THE ENERGY STORE

Energy at the top

The cart is at rest, 6.0 m above the coupling floor. Take the coupling floor as zero height. How much gravitational potential energy does the cart store?

Mass of the cart160 kg
Height above the floor6.0 m
g9.8 m/s²
Door needs at least4,800 J
PE = mgh
CHAPTER 03 · YOUR PHYSICS

Friction’s toll

The jammed brake drags all the way down. Friction does negative work on the cart, so some of its energy becomes heat. Find the energy lost to friction and the kinetic energy the cart still has when it reaches the coupling.

Friction coefficient μ0.10
Horizontal run X12.0 m
Length along the slope d13.4 m
Starts fromrest
Wfriction = μN·d = μ(mg cos θ)d = μmgX  (because d cos θ = X)  ·  KEbottom = PE − Wfriction
CHAPTER 04 · CHOOSE THE COUPLING

Soft, balanced or hard?

The cart reaches the coupling with the kinetic energy you found in Chapter 3. The coupling catches it over Δx = 1.2 m and captures a fraction c of that kinetic energy. The generator turns 85% of the captured energy into electrical energy for the door (efficiency η = 0.85). The door needs at least 4,800 J, and the safety interlock blocks any catch with an average force above 6,100 N. You choose the setting.

Predict first

With this setting, what will the door do?

CHAPTER 04 · THE OUTCOME

CHAPTER 05 · THE LAST RUN

Design the last run

The inner gallery door needs its own pulse of at least 4,800 J, and the cart has been winched back to the top for one last run. The first run scored the rail, so friction is now μ = 0.20, and a 6.0 m drop is no longer enough. Choose a release height h and a capture setting c that pass all four limits. The cart starts from rest, and the horizontal run is still 12.0 m.

Mass of the cart160 kg
Friction coefficient μ0.20
Horizontal run X12.0 m
Coupling stroke Δx1.2 m
KEbottom = mgh − μmgX  ·  Edoor = ηc·KEbottom  ·  F = c·KEbottom ÷ Δx  ·  KE = ½mv²
Limits: Edoor ≥ 4,800 J  ·  F ≤ 6,100 N  ·  speed into the coupling vi ≤ 10.5 m/s  ·  speed out of the coupling vf ≤ 5.2 m/s (the end buffer can’t stop a faster cart)
1 · Minimum release height2 · Approved design
